why_this_exists: This working tree is shared. Codex commits Temporal Gravity work into it while this campaign is mid-integration, and that fact has now produced two distinct failures. Both were silent.

observed_failures.failure: unstaged work reverted by a concurrent git operation
observed_failures.what_happened: A delegated lane's patch was applied and left unstaged while its guards were verified. Codex committed four TG commits in that window and the unstaged changes were gone. `git add` then reported 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'.
observed_failures.cost: the lane's work had to be re-applied, and in between I reported a capability as missing that was present in the patch all along
observed_failures.rule: On a tree another agent commits into, apply and commit are ONE step. Verify after committing, not before. A commit is cheap to amend; work lost to someone else's checkout is not recoverable from the tree.

observed_failures.failure: git apply -3 reported success and wrote nothing
observed_failures.what_happened: `git apply -3` printed 'Applied patch to X cleanly' followed by 'Falling back to direct application...' and left the tree unchanged. A plain `git apply` of the same patch, with `--check` returning 0, applied all 30 files.
observed_failures.cost: I read the resulting tree, found the seventeen YOU events absent, and reported that as a lane failure. They were in the patch the whole time -- 408 lines in crates/hawking-events/src/you_events.rs.
observed_failures.rule: After any apply, confirm a named file from the patch actually exists before drawing any conclusion from the tree. `--stat` lists what SHOULD land; check that something did.

standing_protocol: stage explicit paths, never `git add -A` -- one sweep would pull Codex's in-flight kernel work into a campaign commit
apply and commit atomically; do not leave a delegated patch unstaged while verifying it
after applying, assert a named file exists before reasoning about the tree
audit every commit against the forbidden-path list BEFORE writing it
never touch crates/hawking-core/src/gravity_glm*.rs, metal/, kernels/, shaders/, numeric_parity.rs, cost_ledger.rs -- Codex owns them, and it is actively editing them

verified_across_this_session.commits_audited: every campaign commit checked against the forbidden-path list

the_general_lesson: A shared working tree makes 'I checked the tree' an unreliable claim, because the tree can change underneath a check for reasons unrelated to the work. Both failures here looked like clean outcomes -- a clean working tree, and a successful apply message. Neither was.
